source.title: Moirai 2.0: When Less Is More for Time Series Forecasting
source.authors: Chenghao Liu; Taha İbrahim Aksu; Jun-Cheng Liu; Xu Liu; Han-Shu Yan; Quang Pham; S. Savarese; Doyen Sahoo; Cai-Ming Xiong; Jun-Nan Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests parameter scaling for time-series forecasting models, a new setting, using benchmark forecast metrics rather than language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The scaling experiment in Table 1 reports MASE and CRPS for three Moirai 2.0 sizes. Other benchmark rankings and ablations do not separately test the claim’s scaling behavior and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Table 1 trains three Moirai 2.0 sizes (11.4M, 87.1M, 305M) on the same corpus and recipe and reports held-out zero-shot GIFT-Eval MASE and CRPS. This is a parameter-scaling result in a new modality (time-series forecasting), so it bears on V5. It does not bear on V6, which concerns downstream tasks of language models as scale or pretraining loss grows.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find no benefit from parameter scaling: base and large underperform small on MASE and CRPS. They attribute this to a mismatch between model size and available pretraining data, and call for aligned data scaling. They also note that other time-series studies report benefits from parameter scaling.
record.recipe_differences: A three-size parameter comparison of time-series models using GIFT-Eval MASE and CRPS, not held-out language-model pretraining loss, token/compute scaling, or compute-optimal fitting.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance differs across the tested parameter sizes: the small variant outperforms both larger variants on MASE and CRPS.
record.problems: The scaling evidence covers only three sizes within one time-series model family and reports benchmark metrics rather than pretraining loss; no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: None of the scaling results in Section 5.3, Table 1 were left out.

untested.parts: Data or compute scaling in time series, fitted power-law form, and image, video, repeated-data or transfer regimes. Only three parameter sizes at one fixed corpus and step count were tested.
Not tested: no language-model downstream tasks are evaluated, and there is no relation between pretraining loss and task performance.
Not tested (no shape sweep at fixed parameter count).

missing.what: Ablation v0 to v1 swaps GIFT-Eval Pretrain for the larger new corpus at the small size: MASE 0.9288 to 0.85, CRPS 0.6469 to 0.58. Corpus size and composition change together, so this is not a clean data-scaling test, but it is the paper's only data-side comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Only three sizes, no uncertainty estimates, and differences are small (about 2%), especially small vs base on MASE. Training steps and data were fixed across sizes, so whether data is the bottleneck (the version's own caveat) is unresolved. The reader's V6 label was dropped because the measure is held-out forecasting error within the modality, not language-model downstream tasks. The Moirai 1.0 small/base/large leaderboard results in Figure 2 are prior models and are not rows.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling for language models.
Whether fits from small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture-shape effects at a fixed parameter count.
Tests parameter scaling in time-series forecasting, but not image or video models, other training regimes, or scaling of held-out pretraining loss.
Tests benchmark forecast metrics across three parameter sizes in one model family; does not test downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or establish a fitted predictive relation.
Does not compare fitting choices or exponents, compute-optimal splits, or fitted curves.

relationships.condition: Moirai 2.0 decoder-only time-series models, 11.4M to 305M parameters, fixed 36M-series corpus, 100k steps at batch 256, GIFT-Eval zero-shot
relationships.reason: Both larger sizes are worse on both metrics than the small model (r3–r6), so forecast error does not fall with parameters here. Data was held fixed and may be the bottleneck, which the authors hypothesize but do not test.
relationships.display_finding: Both larger models performed worse on both metrics than the 11.4M model with data fixed, while a data bottleneck remained an untested explanation.
